name: Bookings live in spreadsheets
summary: Keeps the venue's bookings in its own spreadsheet and calendar: holds an enquiry the calendar has room for, flags clashes, logs every change to a booked value so booked revenue stays true, and queues any calendar move or removal for approval. Crons read and draft; a person approves every calendar change.

all.evidence: 7 discovery calls describe this way of booking (6 activity venues, 1 party venue)

covered_by.hold-or-book: hold cron (calendar hold, Clash when busy)
covered_by.amend-or-cancel: changes cron (moves and removals queued for approval)
covered_by.record-keeping: hold and changes crons (Original and Logged value columns, Changes tab)
covered_by.other: skill (money received on the day that differs from the booked value, judged by hand)

crons.name: hold
crons.summary: Hold each new enquiry the venue calendar has room for; mark clashes and unreadable rows Check.

crons.name: changes
crons.summary: Log booked-value changes once to the Changes tab; queue calendar moves and removals for approval (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: rows in the venue's own bookings and changes tabs, a free-busy check, and a hold on the venue calendar with no guests invited. Moving or removing a calendar event waits for a person.

google-workspace.covers: bookings sheet rows, the change log, calendar clash checks and holds, calendar moves and removals (approval only)

gaps: Roller holds most of these bookings (the calls name it on hold-or-book and amend-or-cancel), but the kit has no Roller platform (core/sdk/platforms/roller is absent), so this workflow cannot read or change Roller bookings.
BigQuery is mapped in the kit and five calls use it for booked-revenue reporting, but this workflow keeps its record in the sheet and does not read BigQuery.
Excel: if the venue keeps its book in an Excel workbook, the microsoft-365 workbook table operations could serve the same two crons. Not built: the Microsoft 365 pages show no booking content.

Guest confirmations and reminders (confirm-with-guest, reminder-send) are not built: no Gmail operation is built, because Gmail field names are not in endpoint-map/raw (only the people, sheets and calendar specs are there).
Enquiry intake: the workflow starts from a row the venue marks Enquiry. No enquiry channel (web form, email, phone) is mapped.
Deposits, pre-orders, no-show chasing, seating plans, day sheets, service prep and waitlists: no mapped platform describes them in the docs given. They stay judgment steps or a later build.
Calendar free-busy is a read sent as a POST, but the kit's operation is marked write, so the deploy needs KIT_ALLOW_WRITES=1 for the hold cron to check the calendar.
The Google adapter is docs-only: its field names come from Google's Sheets and Calendar specs, and it has not run against a real Google Workspace account.

evidence.calls: 7 of 7 hospitality discovery calls that discuss bookings describe how they do it; every step is manual
evidence.platforms: Roller's own product and blog pages, mapped step by step; the Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 pages hold no booking content
